title: The Current of the Empty Quarter
premise: Tamsin Sterling, a salvage diver haunted by a wreck the navy erased from its records, is hired by her old rival Cassian Voss to recover a drowned archive from the river city of Meridian Hollow—the same job that got her father killed and their crew sworn to silence. Following the river upstream through smuggler towns, flooded villages, and a militarized source, Tamsin uncovers that the navy sank a civilian settlement to bury evidence of an illegal weapons program, and that the 'debt' she carries is a ledger of victims' names her father died protecting. Betrayed by Voss, who wants the ledger destroyed to protect his own family's complicity, Tamsin must choose between restoring her stolen reputation and delivering justice to people who were never allowed to exist on any record. In the end she floods the source facility's servers with the truth, surrenders her compass—her father's last gift—to the river as a memorial, and finds belonging not in vindication but in the community of the drowned village's survivors who take her in.
about_author: Felix Oyelaran is a former maritime archivist who spent six years cataloguing declassified naval salvage reports before turning to fiction full-time. He writes from a houseboat on a slow brown river, where he claims the best plot twists arrive with the fog.

chapters.title: Salt and Ledger
chapters.summary: Tamsin dives a restricted wreck at night, recovering a corroded strongbox while evading a patrol boat. Her POV establishes her debt to a loan shark and her ritual of reading her father's water-stained compass. Emotional beat: restless competence masking grief.

chapters.title: The Rival's Offer
chapters.summary: Cassian Voss appears at the dockside tavern with a contract: recover a sealed archive from the sunken district of Meridian Hollow. Tamsin refuses; he mentions her father's name. POV alternates briefly to Voss watching her leave. Beat: old wounds reopened.

chapters.title: Crew of Strays
chapters.summary: Tamsin reluctantly recruits her skeleton crew: engineer Odile, ex-navy sonar tech Bram, and teenage deckhand Pip. Each carries a reason to stay invisible. Her POV; the beat is wary family-building over bad coffee and worse odds.

chapters.title: Downriver Rules
chapters.summary: The crew runs the first gauntlet of toll bridges and corrupt harbor police. A near-arrest forces Tamsin to bribe an officer with a salvaged chronometer. Her POV. Beat: the law is a current, not a wall—and it flows against them.

chapters.title: Meridian Hollow
chapters.summary: Arrival at the half-drowned city; streets end in green water. Tamsin recognizes the architecture from her father's forbidden dive logs. Her POV, dread rising. Beat: memory made physical.

chapters.title: What the Navy Won't Discuss
chapters.summary: Bram decrypts a fragment: the wreck Tamsin has been diving matches the Hollow's missing ferry. The navy didn't lose it—it scuttled it. Shared POV via recovered log entries. Beat: vertigo of rewritten history.

chapters.title: First Descent
chapters.summary: Tamsin and Odile dive the submerged archive vault, finding it already breached by someone else. They escape a collapsing stairwell with one intact canister. Tamsin's POV underwater, claustrophobic. Beat: they are not alone in this story.

chapters.title: The Canister
chapters.summary: Inside: a partial ledger of names, dates, and a chemical designation. Tamsin recognizes her father's handwriting annotating the margins. Her POV, hands shaking. Beat: the debt was never money.

chapters.title: Voss's Version
chapters.summary: Voss reveals his grandfather helped run the program; he wants the ledger destroyed before a navy audit surfaces it. He offers Tamsin her father's cleared name in exchange. His POV, genuinely conflicted. Beat: two kinds of shame.

chapters.title: Sworn Off
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Tamsin watches her father leave for the Hollow job and never return; the surviving crew swears silence around a burning boat. Her POV. Beat: the origin of every rule she now breaks.

chapters.title: Upstream
chapters.summary: The crew slips past a navy cordon at night using a decommissioned dredger. Pip asks why they can't just sell the ledger and vanish. Tamsin's POV. Beat: the question she can't answer yet.

chapters.title: Flooded Parish
chapters.summary: They shelter in a church steeple above waterline, finding fresh supplies—someone lives here. First contact with Mara Iles, a survivor of the drowned settlement. Alternating POV. Beat: the dead have descendants, and they remember.

chapters.title: Mara's Testimony
chapters.summary: Mara describes the evacuation that never happened: sirens, locked gates, the ferry that took only officials. The ledger lists her mother. Tamsin's POV, guilt crystallizing. Beat: witness as weight.

chapters.title: Patrol Lights
chapters.summary: A navy gunboat sweeps the parish; the crew hides the canister in a reliquary. Bram nearly drowns covering their exit. His POV. Beat: loyalty tested without words.

chapters.title: The Informer
chapters.summary: Someone signaled the patrol. Suspicion fractures the crew; Voss's man Deke is caught with a transmitter but claims Voss ordered him to mislead the navy, not find them. Tamsin's POV. Beat: trust becomes cargo, easily jettisoned.

chapters.title: Rapids of the Old Locks
chapters.summary: White-knuckle passage through derelict locks; the dredger loses its barge and half their fuel. Odile's POV, furious and brilliant. Beat: competence as love language.

chapters.title: Smugglers' Reach
chapters.summary: Trading fuel for passage with river smugglers, Tamsin learns the source is guarded by a private contractor, not the navy—someone bought the secret. Her POV. Beat: the conspiracy has shareholders.

chapters.title: Compass Reading
chapters.summary: Tamsin finally opens her father's compass casing: inside, a microfilm key matching the ledger's cipher. He meant for someone to finish this. Her POV, weeping at the wheel. Beat: inheritance accepted.

chapters.title: Deke's Confession
chapters.summary: Deke admits Voss hired him to track the ledger's copies, not the crew—but there is another copy, hidden in the Hollow, and Voss's auditors want both burned. Deke's POV. Beat: even traitors have employers.

chapters.title: Split Current
chapters.summary: The crew votes: press to the source or double back for the second copy. Tamsin splits them—she and Pip go upstream; the rest return downstream. Her POV, cold with resolve. Beat: leadership as loneliness.

chapters.title: The Gorge Road
chapters.summary: Tamsin and Pip travel overland through the gorge, dodging contractor drones. Pip confesses he stowed away because his own town was erased by a reservoir project. His POV. Beat: two orphans of official maps.

chapters.title: Checkpoint at Weir Nine
chapters.summary: Caught at a checkpoint, Tamsin talks her way through by posing as a contractor surveyor—using knowledge from her father's notes. Her POV, adrenaline and shame. Beat: passing as the enemy.

chapters.title: Downstream Betrayal
chapters.summary: Voss intercepts Odile, Bram, and Mara, seizing the original canister. Mara escapes with a photostat. Voss's POV, telling himself destruction is mercy. Beat: the rival becomes the antagonist.

chapters.title: Source Country
chapters.summary: Tamsin reaches the headwaters: a fenced facility built over the old research station, discharge pipes bleeding into the spring itself. Her POV, horror quieted into purpose. Beat: the wound at the world's beginning.

chapters.title: Infiltration
chapters.summary: Night entry through the discharge culvert—the same route her father used. She finds his bolt-cutters still wedged in the fence, rusted. Her POV. Beat: following a ghost's footprints.

chapters.title: The Archive Below
chapters.summary: Deep in the facility, Tamsin locates the master records: the program, the scuttled ferry, the order signed by Voss's grandfather. She photographs everything onto the microfilm key. Her POV. Beat: proof at last.

chapters.title: Alarm
chapters.summary: Pip trips a sensor covering their retreat; contractors flood the corridors. Separated, Tamsin hides in a flooding sub-basement as the water rises. Her POV, terror. Beat: the river reclaiming its own.

chapters.title: Drowned Room
chapters.summary: Trapped underwater, Tamsin relives her father's final dive through a recovered helmet-cam file playing on a loop in the dark. She finds the emergency vent he used. Her POV, transcendent fear. Beat: the dead teaching the living to breathe.

chapters.title: Reunion at the Weir
chapters.summary: Tamsin and Pip escape and meet Mara, who has rallied Hollow survivors and sympathetic lock-keepers. Odile arrives battered, reporting Voss has gone to the facility himself. Tamsin's POV. Beat: scattered currents converging.

chapters.title: Voss at the Source
chapters.summary: Voss attempts to purge the servers, but the facility director—protecting his own pension—refuses and takes him hostage along with the data. Voss's POV, stripped of control. Beat: the destroyer captured by his own machine.

chapters.title: The Bargain
chapters.summary: The director offers Tamsin a trade: the ledger originals for her silence and Voss's freedom. She pretends to accept, buying time for Odile to tap the facility's flood-control system. Her POV. Beat: justice wearing a mask.

chapters.title: Opening the Sluices
chapters.summary: Odile and Bram divert the river through the server halls—not to destroy the records, but to force evacuation and expose the facility to outside inspectors already tipped by Mara's network. Odile's POV. Beat: the river as witness.

chapters.title: Standoff in the Rising Water
chapters.summary: Tamsin confronts the director waist-deep in rising water; Voss breaks free and, instead of fleeing, hands her the original canister—he chooses exposure over his family's name. Voss's POV, redeemed at cost. Beat: the rival's last current.

chapters.title: The Flood
chapters.summary: The facility floods; the director is arrested by arriving federal inspectors as systems fail. Tamsin nearly drowns saving the ledger, saved by Pip and Mara hauling her through the breach. Ensemble POV. Beat: climax—truth costs everything and buys more.

chapters.title: Aftermath at the Spring
chapters.summary: Days later: hearings announced, the Hollow's dead named publicly. Tamsin stands at the clean-running source. Her POV, hollowed and light. Beat: victory without triumph.

chapters.title: Settling Accounts
chapters.summary: The loan shark's debt is voided when the navy quietly settles to avoid testimony; Tamsin refuses hush money and donates it to the survivors' fund. Her POV. Beat: refusing the old currency.

chapters.title: The Compass Returned
chapters.summary: Tamsin wades into the Hollow's flooded street and gives her father's compass to the river above where the ferry lies. Mara stands beside her. Her POV. Beat: grief given somewhere to go.

chapters.title: New Charter
chapters.summary: The crew reforms—not as salvagers of secrets but as a recovery service documenting drowned towns for the families left behind. Pip signs on as apprentice. Tamsin's POV. Beat: work as belonging.

chapters.title: Voss's Letter
chapters.summary: Voss, awaiting sentencing, writes asking nothing—only that a marker be placed for his grandfather's victims alongside his name. Tamsin reads it twice and keeps it. Her POV. Beat: forgiveness considered, not granted.

chapters.title: The Current Runs Clear
chapters.summary: One year later, the crew launches from the rebuilt Hollow docks; the river runs clear to the sea. Tamsin casts off with no debts, no secrets, and a crew that chose her. Her POV, closing frame echoing chapter one. Beat: home is a heading, not a place.
